clue.text: Money-taker, I, on remand -a debt to be settled

indicators.note: a debt to be settled must be sorted out, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone on remand faces a debt that must be paid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be settled' is the anagram signal, though it reads as part of the debt story; the hyphen before 'a' is printing noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot machine swallows gamblers' coins, so it is jokingly a taker of cash.

clue.text: First men in, or on?

parts.note: the first batsmen to go in at cricket, or the openings in which things go 'on' (switches, gambits) all start proceedings

explanation.definitionFit: Opening batsmen are the first pair sent in by a cricket side, and an opening move starts things on.

clue.text: Short of a distributor, possibly?

parts.note: 'short' reads as lacking, but here it is a short circuit, which a car's distributor might suffer

explanation.surface: A motorist finds the car lacking a distributor.
explanation.definitionFit: A short circuit is a wiring defect, such as one in an engine's distributor.

clue.text: Collapse of game at home

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A sports fixture falls apart on home ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin as a noun is a downfall or breakdown.

clue.text: One should grow and lose tail to leave a good score

definitions.text: One should grow and lose tail to leave a good score

parts.words: One should grow and lose tail to leave a good score
parts.note: a young bird should grow into the adult; drop the final T of its name and a golf score two under par remains

explanation.surface: A young creature must mature and shed its tail to earn praise.
explanation.walkthrough: The young bird grows into an eagle, and cutting its last letter also leaves EAGLE, two under par in golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bird of prey of the largest kind will mature into an adult; minus its last letter it names a golf score.

clue.text: They make an Italian brood!

parts.note: a brood is a family of youngsters, so the clue wants the Italian word for little children

explanation.surface: A remark on what makes up a big Italian family.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for babies or small children, who together form a brood.

clue.text: No settling for Nanny to MEP on the move?

indicators.note: letters on the move are shifting about, so the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Member of the European Parliament on his travels refuses to pay the nanny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the move' scrambles NANNY, TO and MEP (a Member of the European Parliament).
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to pay is a failure to settle a bill.

clue.text: Handy agenda, it is new in our time

indicators.note: making something new reshapes it, so the preceding letters are put in fresh order

explanation.surface: A practical meeting plan is something novel nowadays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal for HANDY AGENDA IT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning nowadays, in the present era.

clue.text: Close in effort to be fashionable

indicators.note: the word for close goes in the word for effort

parts.note: a try is an effort or attempt
close as a noun is an end

explanation.surface: Approaching something in a stylish attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means in the latest style, up to date.

clue.text: Drawing level late in the day

definitions.meaning: making things equal or flat, as a verb form
the time between afternoon and night

explanation.surface: Catching up with a rival just before nightfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: making equal, and the close of day.

clue.text: Lizard to keep an eye on?

definitions.meaning: a large tropical lizard of Africa, Asia and Australia goes by this name

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a reptile needs watching.
explanation.definitionFit: A large reptile family name, and a verb meaning to observe or supervise.

clue.text: Pier not opened for painter

indicators.note: a word not opened loses its first letter

parts.note: a jetty is a pier or landing stage

explanation.surface: A closed pier is the subject of an artist's work.
explanation.walkthrough: William Etty was a 19th-century English painter, known for nudes.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the English artist William Etty.

clue.text: Drug treatment for Conservative in good offices

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the phrase for good offices

parts.note: good offices means help in settling a dispute, mediation

explanation.surface: Someone in a pleasant workplace gives medicine to a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good offices' is a diplomatic phrase for help in negotiation; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicine given to treat illness is drug treatment.

clue.text: Voice taking key number, completely

parts.note: a number is something that numbs, like the anaesthetic ether

explanation.surface: A singer chooses a key for a song, and it goes perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as 'numb-er', an anaesthetic such as ether; 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether means wholly or totally.

clue.text: This joint in horses can damage itself

indicators.note: to damage the word is to break up its letters

explanation.surface: A horse's joint might injure itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint above the hock in a horse's hind leg, like a knee, has this name.

clue.text: Condemns light in the final period

explanation.surface: A sentence comes down at daybreak at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Judgment Day, the end of the world, is the last time.

clue.text: Up in arms?

parts.note: 'up in arms' usually means angry, but here it means expert in coats of arms

explanation.definitionFit: Relating to coats of arms, as studied by experts in that field.

clue.text: Spiny fish has disappeared into choppy Dart

indicators.note: the word for disappeared goes into the scrambled river
choppy water is churned up, so the river's letters are tossed about

explanation.surface: A spiny fish vanishes in rough water on the Dart, a river in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choppy' rearranges the river's name into DRAT, and 'into' signals the container. The Dart is a river in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fish with spines on its fins.

clue.text: Half-tide sailor in attempt to restore Lot's wife?

indicators.note: only one half of the word tide is kept, its second

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor, at mid-tide, tries to bring back Lot's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' keeps the latter half of tide. Lot's wife turned to a pillar of salt in Genesis, so to restore her you would remove the salt; 'in attempt to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove salt is what a pillar of salt would need to become a woman again.

clue.text: Protein producing a bit of a frenzy, medically speaking

indicators.note: only a portion of the words that follow is used, sitting within them

explanation.surface: A doctor talks about some biochemical sparking a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Enzymes are biological catalysts made of protein.

clue.text: Sides of the Spanish planes?

parts.note: to plane is to smooth, so planes means evens

explanation.surface: Something about the sides of Spanish aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: A side in cricket or football has eleven players, so sides are elevens.
explanation.definitionFit: A team of eleven players is a side.

clue.text: Seafood from southern river, picked early?

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

indicators.note: the early part of the word picked is what's used

explanation.surface: Shellfish from a southern river, harvested before others.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded langoustines are served as this dish.

clue.text: Feel wretched with acne, perhaps? Toleration needed

parts.note: to suffer is to feel wretched

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone miserable with spots needs patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ACNE into ANCE; 'with' and 'needed' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufferance is tolerance, putting up with something.

clue.text: Cricket side at church, long ago

parts.note: the on side is a half of the cricket field
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A cricket team played beside the church years back.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side (leg side) is one half of the field; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some past time.

clue.text: King of the cabbages?

parts.note: the nursery-rhyme king (old and merry) shares his name with a cabbage plant

explanation.definitionFit: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme, and a word for cabbage or kale.

clue.text: Huge lad, shaking, split his sides

indicators.note: the words are shaken up, so their letters change places

explanation.surface: A big boy, shaking with mirth, burst out.
explanation.definitionFit: To split one's sides is to roar with mirth.

clue.text: Make fast time where anchor is dropped

parts.note: to moor a boat is to make it fast
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Tie up quickly when the anchor goes over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make fast' looks like 'hurry' but means secure a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A place to tie up or anchor a ship.

clue.text: Winning ways of fair head?

explanation.surface: Charming manners of a blond person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland, a ness as in Loch Ness; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm, an appealing quality, is what makes someone win others over.
